issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify a SealSaloon constructor taking a String parameter (SealSaloon(String)) for the saloon name, but the template usage (Main.java) and the provided solution implement and use a no-argument constructor SealSaloon(). This contradiction leaves students unclear whether to implement a constructor that accepts a name (and whether to store it as a field and provide a getter) or to implement a no-arg constructor as shown in the examples.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the constructor requirement across artifacts. Either: (A) Update the template and solution to provide a SealSaloon(String name) constructor that stores the name in a private field (with a getter) as described in the problem statement and UML; or (B) Update the problem statement and UML to specify a no-argument constructor (SealSaloon()) and remove the requirement to pass/store a name. Ensure example usage in Main.java matches the chosen constructor signature.

issues.description: Constructor signature mismatch for SealSaloon: the problem statement UML and text specify a constructor SealSaloon(String) taking the saloon name, but both the provided template usage (Main) and the solution implement/use a no-argument constructor SealSaloon(). This discrepancy can confuse students about the required API and where to provide the saloon name.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the constructor API: either update the problem statement to require a no-argument constructor SealSaloon() (matching template Main and the solution), or modify the code to provide a SealSaloon(String name) constructor (and update Main and the solution to pass the name). Choose one consistent constructor signature and reflect it in the UML, textual description, and the code.
